To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the calibration of pulse wave signals to blood pressure is still an unsolved problem and that the accuracy of ambulatory blood pressure measurement is still limited by the acquisition and processing of signals.

the accuracy of blood pressure measurement systems based on pulse transit/arrival time can be improved by the use of alternative technologies and locations for the measurement, by improved signal processing and by the integration of these systems into ambulatory blood pressure monitor systems.

the accuracy of pulse wave transit/arrival time based blood pressure monitoring is limited by the acquisition and processing of pulse wave signals, the changes in vascular tone, the pre-ejection phase and the calibration of the pulse wave transit/ arrival time to the blood pressure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a new ambulatory blood pressure monitor based on pulse transit/arrival time.
the development of a new ambulatory blood pressure monitor based on pulse arrival time.
improving the accuracy of ambulatory blood pressure measurements using pulse transit or arrival times.

the research community has not yet been able to design an accurate, reliable and fully integrated ambulatory blood pressure monitor.
the research in the field of blood pressure monitoring based on PTA is still in its infancy and needs to be further developed in order to achieve a reliable blood pressure measurement.
the current state of the art is not yet mature enough to provide accurate and reliable ambulatory blood pressure measurement.

the accuracy of current ambulatory blood pressures monitors is limited and that further research is needed in order to improve these devices.
there is still a need for further investigation of blood pressure monitors using pulse transit or arrival times in order to achieve the required accuracy for ambulatory blood pressure measurement.
the accuracy of the pulse transit/arrival time-based blood pressure monitors is still insufficient and that further research is necessary to improve the accuracy and the usability of these devices.

the design of ambulatory blood pressure systems requires an interdisciplinary approach.
